events.title: Herschel discovers two moons of Uranus
events.description: Astronomer William Herschel spotted Titania and Oberon, the two largest moons of Uranus. He made the discovery only a few years after finding the planet itself.
events.significance: These were the first moons found orbiting Uranus. They showed that the newly identified planet had a system of satellites, as Jupiter and Saturn do.

events.title: Grand Canyon protected as a national monument
events.description: President Theodore Roosevelt proclaimed the Grand Canyon a U.S. national monument. The proclamation shielded the vast chasm in Arizona from mining claims and exploitation.
events.significance: The proclamation was a landmark in American conservation. It paved the way for Grand Canyon National Park, which was established in 1919.

events.title: Insulin is first given to a human patient
events.description: In Toronto, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson, who was dying of diabetes, received the first injection of insulin. The treatment had been developed by Frederick Banting, Charles Best and their colleagues.
events.significance: Insulin turned type 1 diabetes from a fatal diagnosis into a manageable condition. It has saved millions of lives since.

events.title: Amelia Earhart flies solo from Hawaii to California
events.description: Amelia Earhart took off from Honolulu and flew alone to Oakland, California. She was the first person to make this solo flight across the Pacific.
events.significance: The flight made Earhart a pioneer among aviators. It also showed the growing reach of long-distance flight.
